key_insight: The paper tracks a rigid target in 3D from single-source far-field measurements by combining analytical scattering updates with Bayesian optimization over translation and rotation across time.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical framework for remote sensing, surveillance, and nondestructive evaluation when only limited far-field data are available and the object is moving.
method: Derive far-field pattern formulas for target translation and rotation in 3D.
Model translational and rotational motion as independent stochastic processes and solve sequential tracking with Bayesian optimization.
Use a fully connected neural network to identify an unknown shape at the initial time from a precomputed dataset.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments that validate the framework and also establishes posterior consistency for the probabilistic model.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of the precomputed shape dataset and on how well the motion assumptions match real target dynamics.
paper_title: Bayesian optimization approach for tracking a moving target from far-field data in three dimensions
